1 # architecture.md 2 3 ## Project Architecture Overview 4 5 **hevy-mcp** is a [Model Context Protocol (MCP)](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/) server for the [Hevy](https://www.hevyapp.com/) fitness API. It lets AI assistants read, analyze, create, and update workouts, routines, exercise templates, and body measurements through authenticated Hevy API requests [[1]](https://app.dosu.dev/documents/86385d8b-fd28-42af-bebd-e017cd533d92). 6 7 The codebase is a TypeScript monorepo organized as a **private workspace orchestrator** with six packages under `packages/`. The root has no runtime `src/` tree — all implementation lives in the workspaces [[2]](https://app.dosu.dev/documents/947ebc0f-60be-4a4e-b227-238f01cd75a6). 8 9 The defining architectural property is that a **single MCP tool contract runs identically on two very different runtimes**: 10 11 ```text 12 Hosted: AI assistant → Streamable HTTP → Cloudflare Worker → Hevy API 13 Local: AI assistant → MCP over stdio → local hevy-mcp → Hevy API 14 ``` 15 16 [[3]](https://app.dosu.dev/documents/86385d8b-fd28-42af-bebd-e017cd533d92) 17 18 This is achieved by keeping the tool implementations and API client runtime-neutral, then composing them into runtime-specific adapters (Node.js and Cloudflare Workers) that never share code with each other [[4]](https://app.dosu.dev/documents/52dd122f-29f8-46dd-9513-3476b4dbb3ae). 19 20 The six workspaces and their roles at a glance: 21 22 | Workspace | Package name | Role | 23 | ---------------------- | ----------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------- | 24 | `packages/hevy-client` | `@hevy-mcp/hevy-client` | Runtime-neutral API client (Kubb-generated) | 25 | `packages/operations` | `@hevy-mcp/operations` | Runtime-neutral shared operations layer | 26 | `packages/core` | `@hevy-mcp/core` | Runtime-neutral MCP tools and server construction | 27 | `packages/node` | `hevy-mcp` | Node.js stdio/HTTP adapter — the only publishable workspace | 28 | `packages/worker` | `@hevy-mcp/worker` | Private Cloudflare Worker HTTP/OAuth adapter | 29 | `packages/cli` | `@chrisdoc/hevy-cli` | Public Hevy command-line client | 30 31 [[5]](https://app.dosu.dev/documents/947ebc0f-60be-4a4e-b227-238f01cd75a6) 32 33 ## Workspace Dependency Diagram 34 35 The shipped composition graph flows from the runtime-neutral packages outward to the platform adapters and public CLI [[6]](https://app.dosu.dev/documents/52dd122f-29f8-46dd-9513-3476b4dbb3ae): 36 37 ```mermaid 38 graph TD 39 HC["@hevy-mcp/hevy-client
runtime-neutral API client"] 40 OPS["@hevy-mcp/operations
runtime-neutral operations layer"] 41 CORE["@hevy-mcp/core
runtime-neutral MCP tools & server"] 42 NODE["hevy-mcp
Node.js stdio/HTTP adapter"] 43 WORKER["@hevy-mcp/worker
Cloudflare Worker HTTP/OAuth adapter"] 44 CLI["@chrisdoc/hevy-cli
public CLI"] 45 46 HC --> OPS 47 HC --> CORE 48 OPS --> CORE 49 CORE --> NODE 50 CORE --> WORKER 51 CORE --> CLI 52 53 style HC fill:#d4edda,stroke:#28a745 54 style OPS fill:#d4edda,stroke:#28a745 55 style CORE fill:#d4edda,stroke:#28a745 56 style NODE fill:#cce5ff,stroke:#004085 57 style WORKER fill:#fff3cd,stroke:#856404 58 style CLI fill:#cce5ff,stroke:#004085 59 ``` 60 61 **Legend:** Green = runtime-neutral · Blue = Node.js adapter · Amber = Cloudflare adapter 62 63 Key constraints to observe in this diagram [[7]](https://app.dosu.dev/documents/947ebc0f-60be-4a4e-b227-238f01cd75a6): 64 65 - `hevy-client`, `operations`, and `core` are **runtime-neutral**: they contain no Node.js built-ins and no Cloudflare-specific bindings, making them safe to import and execute in either runtime. 66 - `hevy-mcp` (Node) and `@hevy-mcp/worker` (Cloudflare) both consume `core` but **must never import each other**. This boundary is enforced by the `package-boundaries` validation lane [[8]](https://github.com/chrisdoc/hevy-mcp/blob/c4ac07dbe84a7e83ba88a5073f0a83ab34af5c86/repository/validation-lanes.json#L209-L227). 67 - `@chrisdoc/hevy-cli` bundles the runtime-neutral packages directly and does **not** depend on either adapter. 68 - `@hevy-mcp/core` depends on both `@hevy-mcp/hevy-client` and `@hevy-mcp/operations` [[9]](https://github.com/chrisdoc/hevy-mcp/blob/47eac6bd864bbfc1d66bbd48881df895e1a4214e/packages/core/package.json#L20-L24); `@hevy-mcp/operations` depends on `@hevy-mcp/hevy-client` [[10]](https://github.com/chrisdoc/hevy-mcp/blob/47eac6bd864bbfc1d66bbd48881df895e1a4214e/packages/operations/package.json#L16-L18). 69 70 > [!IMPORTANT] 71 > The adapter packages (`hevy-mcp` and `@hevy-mcp/worker`) must never import one another. Violating this constraint would pull Node-specific or Cloudflare-specific code into the wrong runtime bundle and cause hard failures at runtime. 72 73 ## Runtime-Neutral vs. Platform Adapters 74 75 ### What "runtime-neutral" means 76 77 A package is **runtime-neutral** when it makes no assumptions about the JavaScript host environment. Concretely, this means: 78 79 - **No Node.js built-ins**: `process`, `fs`, `child_process`, `path`, `crypto` (Node's version), etc. are forbidden. 80 - **No Cloudflare-specific bindings**: KV namespaces, Durable Objects, environment secrets injected via `env` object, and Worker-specific globals are forbidden. 81 - **Standard Web APIs only**: `fetch`, `URL`, `TextEncoder`, `crypto` (Web Crypto), and the rest of the [WinterCG](https://wintercg.org/) baseline. 82 83 The two packages that must satisfy this constraint are `packages/hevy-client` and `packages/core` [[11]](https://app.dosu.dev/documents/52dd122f-29f8-46dd-9513-3476b4dbb3ae). The `packages/operations` layer also sits in this neutral zone — it depends only on `hevy-client` and adds no platform imports [[10]](https://github.com/chrisdoc/hevy-mcp/blob/47eac6bd864bbfc1d66bbd48881df895e1a4214e/packages/operations/package.json#L16-L18). 84 85 ### The adapter pattern 86 87 Platform-specific concerns are isolated to the adapter packages: 88 89 | Package | Owns | 90 | ----------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | 91 | `packages/node` | stdio transport, local Streamable HTTP transport, process lifecycle (`SIGTERM`/`SIGINT`), Node telemetry (Sentry, OTLP), stdio observability, update checks | 92 | `packages/worker` | Cloudflare Worker HTTP entrypoint, Streamable HTTP handler, OAuth 2.1 layer (KV-backed), Cloudflare bindings and environment types | 93 94 [[12]](https://app.dosu.dev/documents/52dd122f-29f8-46dd-9513-3476b4dbb3ae) 95 96 ### Enforcement 97 98 The `package-boundaries` lane (blocking, runs on Node 24 and 26) uses dependency-cruiser to statically validate that the boundary rules hold across the entire workspace graph [[8]](https://github.com/chrisdoc/hevy-mcp/blob/c4ac07dbe84a7e83ba88a5073f0a83ab34af5c86/repository/validation-lanes.json#L209-L227). A pull request that introduces a Node built-in into `packages/core` or a Cloudflare binding into `packages/hevy-client` will fail CI before merge. 99 100 > [!NOTE] 101 > `packages/node/src/utils/stdio-observability.ts` is a deliberate exception: it resides in the Node adapter and instruments private MCP SDK internals. The runtime-neutral packages themselves remain clean; see [Key Design Decisions](#key-design-decisions) for details on the stdio observability tradeoff. 102 103 ## Why This Structure Exists 104 105 ### One tool contract, two runtimes 106 107 The primary motivation is to expose the same 26 MCP tools to users regardless of whether they run the server locally via npm or connect to the hosted Cloudflare endpoint. Splitting implementation into runtime-neutral packages and thin adapters is the only way to achieve this without duplicating logic [[13]](https://app.dosu.dev/documents/86385d8b-fd28-42af-bebd-e017cd533d92). 108 109 ### Preventing invalid bundles 110 111 Bundling Node.js code (anything that imports `process`, `fs`, `os`, etc.) into a Cloudflare Worker will fail at deploy time or produce silent runtime errors. Conversely, shipping Cloudflare bindings inside the published npm package would make it non-functional on a developer's machine. The strict layer boundary eliminates both failure modes at the source [[12]](https://app.dosu.dev/documents/52dd122f-29f8-46dd-9513-3476b4dbb3ae). 112 113 ### Clean published surface 114 115 Only one workspace is publishable to npm: `hevy-mcp` (the Node adapter). Everything else is either a private internal package or a separate public package: 116 117 | Package | Published? | Why | 118 | ----------------------- | ---------- | --------------------------------------- | 119 | `hevy-mcp` | ✅ npm | The user-facing Node.js MCP server | 120 | `@chrisdoc/hevy-cli` | ✅ npm | Public standalone CLI | 121 | `@hevy-mcp/core` | ❌ private | Internal; bundled into both adapters | 122 | `@hevy-mcp/hevy-client` | ❌ private | Internal; bundled into both adapters | 123 | `@hevy-mcp/operations` | ❌ private | Internal; bundled into both adapters | 124 | `@hevy-mcp/worker` | ❌ private | Deployed directly to Cloudflare Workers | 125 126 [[14]](https://app.dosu.dev/documents/52dd122f-29f8-46dd-9513-3476b4dbb3ae) 127 128 ### Private versioning for release/deployment identity 129 130 The private workspaces (`core`, `hevy-client`, `operations`, `worker`) are still versioned using Changesets. This provides internal release and deployment identity — for example, knowing exactly which `@hevy-mcp/core` version is running in production — without ever creating npm tags (`privatePackages.tag=false`) [[14]](https://app.dosu.dev/documents/52dd122f-29f8-46dd-9513-3476b4dbb3ae). 131 132 > [!NOTE] 133 > Worker deployment happens only when a Changesets version commit changes `packages/worker/package.json`. Public Node or CLI releases do not trigger a Worker deploy; Worker-only private releases still do [[15]](https://app.dosu.dev/documents/52dd122f-29f8-46dd-9513-3476b4dbb3ae). 134 135 ## Changeset Cascade 136 137 Because the private packages are bundled into the published adapters, a change in a shared package must version-bump every downstream consumer. This "cascade" is enforced by the `package-changesets` CI lane (`npm run check:changeset`), which uses the `release-cascade` comparison from `repository/validation-lanes.json` as its machine-readable source of truth [[16]](https://github.com/chrisdoc/hevy-mcp/blob/c4ac07dbe84a7e83ba88a5073f0a83ab34af5c86/repository/validation-lanes.json#L259-L273). 138 139 ### Cascade rules 140 141 ```mermaid 142 flowchart TD 143 Q["Which package did you change?"] 144 145 Q --> HC["@hevy-mcp/hevy-client"] 146 Q --> OPS["@hevy-mcp/operations"] 147 Q --> CORE["@hevy-mcp/core"] 148 Q --> NODE["packages/node
(hevy-mcp)"] 149 Q --> WORKER["packages/worker
OR cloudflare.config.ts"] 150 Q --> CLI["packages/cli
(@chrisdoc/hevy-cli)"] 151 152 HC --> HC_BUMPS["Bump: hevy-client,
operations, core,
hevy-mcp, worker, CLI"] 153 OPS --> OPS_BUMPS["Bump: operations,
core, hevy-mcp,
worker, CLI"] 154 CORE --> CORE_BUMPS["Bump: core,
hevy-mcp, worker, CLI"] 155 NODE --> NODE_BUMPS["Bump: hevy-mcp only"] 156 WORKER --> WORKER_BUMPS["Bump: @hevy-mcp/worker only"] 157 CLI --> CLI_BUMPS["Bump: @chrisdoc/hevy-cli only"] 158 159 style HC_BUMPS fill:#fce4ec 160 style OPS_BUMPS fill:#fce4ec 161 style CORE_BUMPS fill:#fce4ec 162 style NODE_BUMPS fill:#e8f5e9 163 style WORKER_BUMPS fill:#e8f5e9 164 style CLI_BUMPS fill:#e8f5e9 165 ``` 166 167 The full matrix [[17]](https://app.dosu.dev/documents/52dd122f-29f8-46dd-9513-3476b4dbb3ae) [[18]](https://app.dosu.dev/documents/947ebc0f-60be-4a4e-b227-238f01cd75a6): 168 169 | Changed package | Required changeset packages | 170 | --------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | 171 | `@hevy-mcp/hevy-client` | `@hevy-mcp/hevy-client`, `@hevy-mcp/operations`, `@hevy-mcp/core`, `hevy-mcp`, `@hevy-mcp/worker`, `@chrisdoc/hevy-cli` | 172 | `@hevy-mcp/operations` | `@hevy-mcp/operations`, `@hevy-mcp/core`, `hevy-mcp`, `@hevy-mcp/worker`, `@chrisdoc/hevy-cli` | 173 | `@hevy-mcp/core` | `@hevy-mcp/core`, `hevy-mcp`, `@hevy-mcp/worker`, `@chrisdoc/hevy-cli` | 174 | Node adapter only | `hevy-mcp` only | 175 | Worker only (or `cloudflare.config.ts`) | `@hevy-mcp/worker` only | 176 | CLI only | `@chrisdoc/hevy-cli` only | 177 178 ### Concrete examples 179 180 | Change | Packages touched | Required changeset packages | 181 | --------------------------------------- | ------------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------- | 182 | Adding a new MCP tool | `packages/core` | `@hevy-mcp/core`, `hevy-mcp`, `@hevy-mcp/worker`, `@chrisdoc/hevy-cli` | 183 | Fixing a bug in the Hevy client wrapper | `packages/hevy-client` | All six packages | 184 | Updating Worker OAuth logic | `packages/worker` | `@hevy-mcp/worker` only | 185 | Adding a CLI subcommand | `packages/cli` | `@chrisdoc/hevy-cli` only | 186 | Updating `cloudflare.config.ts` | (root, Worker release trigger) | `@hevy-mcp/worker` only | 187 188 ### How it is enforced 189 190 CI runs `npm run check:changeset` (`npx changeset status --since=origin/`) as a blocking gate on every pull request [[19]](https://app.dosu.dev/documents/947ebc0f-60be-4a4e-b227-238f01cd75a6). The `package-changesets` lane checks that every changed workspace directory has a changeset file that names that package, then applies the transitive composition matrix. The `release-cascade` comparison label in `repository/validation-lanes.json` is the machine-readable definition driving this check [[20]](https://github.com/chrisdoc/hevy-mcp/blob/c4ac07dbe84a7e83ba88a5073f0a83ab34af5c86/repository/validation-lanes.json#L259-L287). 191 192 > [!IMPORTANT] 193 > The Conventional Commit type (`chore:`, `docs:`, etc.) does **not** determine changeset eligibility. What matters is whether the change touches a file under `packages/*`, modifies runtime-visible behaviour, changes a workspace dependency, or updates an explicit release trigger like `cloudflare.config.ts` [[21]](https://app.dosu.dev/documents/947ebc0f-60be-4a4e-b227-238f01cd75a6). 194 195 ## Key Design Decisions 196 197 ### Generated API client via Kubb 198 199 The Hevy API client, TypeScript types, and Zod schemas under `packages/hevy-client/src/generated/` are produced by [Kubb](https://kubb.dev/) from the Hevy OpenAPI specification [[22]](https://app.dosu.dev/documents/52dd122f-29f8-46dd-9513-3476b4dbb3ae). The generation pipeline is: 200 201 ```bash 202 npm run openapi # fetch upstream Hevy spec → openapi-spec.json 203 npm run build:client # run Kubb → packages/hevy-client/src/generated/ 204 ``` 205 206 > [!WARNING] 207 > **Never edit files in `packages/hevy-client/src/generated/` by hand.** All generated TypeScript errors in that directory are expected and should be ignored. Fixes belong in `scripts/openapi-spec.js` (applied before spec write) so they survive future regenerations [[23]](https://app.dosu.dev/documents/947ebc0f-60be-4a4e-b227-238f01cd75a6). 208 209 Only the curated package barrels (`@hevy-mcp/hevy-client/types` and `@hevy-mcp/hevy-client/schemas`) are the public API of the client package. Generated API functions and `.kubb` internals are private [[24]](https://app.dosu.dev/documents/947ebc0f-60be-4a4e-b227-238f01cd75a6). 210 211 ### Zod schema inference for type-safe tool parameters 212 213 All MCP tool handlers use **Zod schema inference** via the `InferToolParams` utility from `packages/core/src/utils/tool-helpers.ts`. This eliminates manual type assertions and ensures parameter types always match their validation schemas [[25]](https://app.dosu.dev/documents/947ebc0f-60be-4a4e-b227-238f01cd75a6). 214 215 ```typescript 216 import type { InferToolParams } from "../utils/tool-helpers.js"; 217 218 const getRoutinesSchema = { 219 page: z.coerce.number().int().gte(1).default(1), 220 pageSize: z.coerce.number().int().gte(1).lte(10).default(5), 221 } as const; 222 223 type GetRoutinesParams = InferToolParams; 224 // ↑ Types are automatically derived — no manual interface needed 225 ``` 226 227 See [TYPE_SAFETY_GUIDE.md](./TYPE_SAFETY_GUIDE.md) for the complete pattern, including `createTypedToolHandler` and response-formatter co-location rules. 228 229 > [!NOTE] 230 > Never use `args as { ... }` type assertions, `Record` in handler signatures, or define parameter types separately from their Zod schemas. These patterns break the single-source-of-truth contract and defeat compile-time safety [[26]](https://app.dosu.dev/documents/947ebc0f-60be-4a4e-b227-238f01cd75a6). 231 232 ### Centralized error handling via `withErrorHandling` 233 234 Every MCP tool handler is wrapped with `withErrorHandling` from `packages/core/src/utils/error-handler.ts`. This utility: 235 236 - Catches all handler errors and converts them to standardized `isError: true` MCP responses. 237 - Preserves the full TypeScript parameter types of the wrapped function. 238 - Attaches a `context` string used in error diagnostics. 239 240 ```typescript 241 server.registerTool( 242 "get-routines", 243 { description: "...", inputSchema: z.object(getRoutinesSchema) }, 244 withErrorHandling(async (args: GetRoutinesParams) => { 245 // handler body 246 }, "get-routines"), 247 ); 248 ``` 249 250 [[27]](https://app.dosu.dev/documents/947ebc0f-60be-4a4e-b227-238f01cd75a6) 251 252 ### MCP SDK internals dependency for stdio observability 253 254 `packages/node/src/utils/stdio-observability.ts` instruments **private MCP SDK stdio fields** to provide raw chunk observability that is not exposed through the SDK's public API [[28]](https://app.dosu.dev/documents/52dd122f-29f8-46dd-9513-3476b4dbb3ae): 255 256 - `_ondata` — wrapped to capture incoming chunk byte length and BOM detection before forwarding. 257 - `_readBuffer` — accessed to replace `readMessage` with an instrumented parser hook. 258 - `_buffer` — read and rewritten during newline-delimited message extraction. 259 260 [[29]](https://github.com/chrisdoc/hevy-mcp/blob/c4ac07dbe84a7e83ba88a5073f0a83ab34af5c86/packages/node/src/utils/stdio-observability.ts#L41-L67) 261 262 The adapter is **fail-closed**: if the private fields are absent (e.g., after an SDK refactor), instrumentation is silently skipped and the original transport is returned unchanged [[30]](https://github.com/chrisdoc/hevy-mcp/blob/c4ac07dbe84a7e83ba88a5073f0a83ab34af5c86/packages/node/src/utils/stdio-observability.ts#L86-L90). 263 264 > [!WARNING] 265 > This is a deliberate architectural tradeoff: private SDK field access provides critical stdio observability that cannot be obtained otherwise, but it means SDK upgrades need careful testing. **Always re-run the complete stdio observability test suite (`npm run test:stdio`) after every MCP TypeScript SDK package upgrade** and inspect the SDK compatibility assumptions before merging [[31]](https://app.dosu.dev/documents/52dd122f-29f8-46dd-9513-3476b4dbb3ae). 266 267 ## Related Documentation 268 269 | Document | What it covers | 270 | ---------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | 271 | [CONTRIBUTING.md](../CONTRIBUTING.md) | Development workflow, environment setup, testing lanes, PR requirements, and changeset rules | 272 | [TYPE_SAFETY_GUIDE.md](./TYPE_SAFETY_GUIDE.md) | Type safety patterns, `InferToolParams` usage, API client barrel imports, and response-formatter co-location | 273 | [test-lanes.md](./test-lanes.md) | Testing strategy, lane ownership, and which lane covers which package or concern | 274 | `deployment-modes.md` | _(forthcoming)_ Detailed coverage of Node stdio, Node HTTP, Cloudflare Worker HTTP, and OAuth deployment modes | 275 276 For the machine-readable source of truth on CI validation, see [`repository/validation-lanes.json`](../repository/validation-lanes.json) [[32]](https://github.com/chrisdoc/hevy-mcp/blob/c4ac07dbe84a7e83ba88a5073f0a83ab34af5c86/repository/validation-lanes.json#L1-L15), which defines all blocking and informational lanes, runtime matrices, and aggregate workflows used by CI and pre-push hooks.

content.text: I’ve also found an important architectural wrinkle: the existing `operations` module is a one-operation pilot, while most MCP and CLI behavior still calls the Hevy client directly. That leaves a shallow middle module and duplicated domain rules—the exact “deepen or delete” decision the final architecture should make explicit.

# MCP TypeScript SDK Examples (Server)

This directory contains runnable MCP server examples built with `@modelcontextprotocol/server` plus framework adapters:

  * `@modelcontextprotocol/express`
  * `@modelcontextprotocol/hono`

For client examples, see `../client/README.md`. For guided docs, see `../../docs/server.md`.

## Running examples

From anywhere in the SDK:
    
    pnpm install
    pnpm --filter @modelcontextprotocol/examples-server exec tsx src/simpleStreamableHttp.ts

Or, from within this package:
    
    cd examples/server
    pnpm tsx src/simpleStreamableHttp.ts

## Example index

Form elicitation server  | Collects non-sensitive user input via schema-driven forms.  | `src/elicitationFormExample.ts`
URL elicitation server  | Secure browser-based flows for sensitive input (API keys, OAuth, payments).  | `src/elicitationUrlExample.ts`

## Multi-node deployment patterns

When deploying MCP servers in a horizontally scaled environment (multiple server instances), there are a few different options that can be useful for different use cases:

  * Stateless mode - no need to maintain state between calls.
  * Persistent storage mode - state stored in a database; any node can handle a session.
  * Local state with message routing - stateful nodes + pub/sub routing for a session.

## Summary

`WebStandardStreamableHTTPServerTransport` validates the `Accept` header with raw substring checks. As a result, invalid media types such as `application/jsonx` and `text/event-stream-bogus` satisfy the transport requirements and are accepted as though the client had listed `application/json` and `text/event-stream`.

This affects both POST negotiation and the GET SSE check.

## Reproduction

On current `main` (`24be4040`), send an initialize request with:
The `Accept` checks still use the older substring behavior.

## Expected behavior

The transport should require the exact concrete media types named by the MCP Streamable HTTP requirements:

  * GET: `text/event-stream`
  * POST: both `application/json` and `text/event-stream`

Parameters and case variants should remain valid, for example:
    
    Accept: Application/JSON; q=0.9, text/event-stream; charset=utf-8

Values that only contain the required strings as substrings should return 406.

## Suggested fix

Parse the comma-separated `Accept` values and compare each media-type essence (`type/subtype`, case-insensitive, without parameters) to the required concrete values. Add regression coverage for POST and GET substring false positives plus valid parameterized media types.

opened on Apr 4, 2026

Issue body actions

## Description

MCP sessions served by `StreamableHTTPServerTransport` are destroyed when the underlying TCP connection closes due to the Node.js default `keepAliveTimeout` (5 seconds). Subsequent requests with a valid `Mcp-Session-Id` receive a 400 "Session not found" error.

This is a regression introduced between SDK versions 1.24.x and 1.27.x. Sessions should survive across independent HTTP requests — the `Mcp-Session-Id` header is the continuity mechanism, not a persistent TCP connection.

For stdio servers, {@linkcode @modelcontextprotocol/server!server/mcp.McpServer#close | server.close()} is sufficient:

## Deployment

### DNS rebinding protection

Under normal circumstances, cross-origin browser restrictions limit what a malicious website can do to your localhost server. DNS rebinding attacks get around those restrictions entirely by making the requests appear as same-origin, since the attacking domain resolves to localhost. Validating the host header on the server side protects against this scenario. All localhost MCP servers should use DNS rebinding protection.

The recommended approach is to use {@linkcode @modelcontextprotocol/express!express.createMcpExpressApp | createMcpExpressApp()} (from `@modelcontextprotocol/express`) or {@linkcode @modelcontextprotocol/hono!hono.createMcpHonoApp | createMcpHonoApp()} (from `@modelcontextprotocol/hono`), which enable Host header validation by default:

# Transport

Last updated Jul 27, 2026|Copy as Markdown|View as Markdown|Agent setup

[Select]

The Model Context Protocol (MCP) specification defines two standard transport mechanisms ↗ for communication between clients and servers:

  1. stdio — Communication over standard in and standard out, designed for local MCP connections.
  2. Streamable HTTP — The standard transport method for remote MCP connections, introduced ↗ in March 2025. It uses a single HTTP endpoint for bidirectional messaging.

Note

Server-Sent Events (SSE) was previously used for remote MCP connections but has been deprecated in favor of Streamable HTTP. Existing `McpAgent` deployments can retain SSE temporarily while they migrate, but new servers should use the stateless Streamable HTTP handler.

MCP servers built with the Agents SDK use `createMcpHandler` to handle Streamable HTTP transport.

issues.title: refactor: track architecture review findings across runtime and tooling
issues.body:
## Outcome

Turn the 2026-08-07 architecture review into owned implementation work without duplicating the existing roadmap. Each finding should either be routed to an existing issue, receive a focused successor issue, or be explicitly deferred with evidence.

The desired end state is less cross-module policy duplication, shorter validation feedback, deeper runtime-neutral operations, simpler runtime/test internals, and a more navigable repository control plane.

## Review baseline

- Repository snapshot: `origin/main` at `2443cad60f74c21ec38592d2083e7fac1398401a`.
- Exact local PR lane: `mise exec -- npm run test:pr -- --outputStyle=stream`.
- Cold run: **62.1s**; warm run: **33.0s**.
- The cold Nx report attributed **33.8s / 55%** to recoverable work; the warm report still attributed **13.8s / 43%**.
- `test:unit` selected 76 files / 842 tests. The contract, stdio, and CLI lanes added 13 file executions whose files were already selected by unit.
- The review was read-only: the source checkout and dedicated review worktree remained clean.

## Findings and current ownership

| # | Finding | Strength | Current owner / review delta |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | One runtime-neutral endpoint policy module | **Strong — top recommendation** | Adjacent to #928, but not owned there as a cross-runtime source for retry semantics, expected 404s, safe diagnostics, and metric endpoint identity. Keep #928 responsible for failure reporting and telemetry ownership. |
| 2 | Complete the shared Hevy operations module | **Strong** | Continue #872. The workspace currently shares `workouts.list`; Core and CLI still independently implement other pagination, read, mutation, search, and aggregation workflows. |
| 3 | Make PR validation artifact-aware and disjoint | **Strong** | Continue #882 with the measured baseline above. Unit overlaps focused lanes, and package/performance paths rebuild artifacts already produced earlier in the graph. |
| 4 | Collapse Node lifecycle into one runner | **Strong** | Continue #878. The stdio and HTTP paths still repeat process tracking, cancellation, config, run spans, update scheduling, shutdown, telemetry flush, and failure classification. |
| 5 | Deepen deterministic MCP test support | **Strong** | Reassess #606, which is closed as `not_planned`. The two mocked integration suites still repeat server/client/runtime registration, in-memory transport, network isolation, and teardown; Core tool tests also repeat registration/handler discovery. |
| 6 | Compile and partition response contracts | **Worth exploring** | No direct issue found; #874 is adjacent but owns public MCP contract projection, not this private implementation. `response-contracts.ts` is 1,252 lines, constructs a Zod object during each render, and repeats pagination mechanics. Benchmark before claiming material runtime gain. |
| 7 | Measure Worker request admission before caching | **Speculative** | Continue #879. Every Worker POST currently performs an upstream `/v1/user/info` validation and creates/connects a new server and transport. Add a repeated-request Worker benchmark before considering any bounded reuse. |
| 8 | Deepen the repository control plane | **Worth exploring** | #873 is complete and #882 is adjacent, but residual duplication remains across control-plane validation, lane rendering, Nx metadata, selectors, and handwritten docs. Current onboarding still says five workspaces instead of six and references deleted paths. |

## Evidence by finding

### 1. Endpoint policy duplication

Relevant files:

- `packages/hevy-client/src/hevy-client-kubb.ts`
- `packages/core/src/utils/hevy-error-policy.ts`
- `packages/core/src/utils/error-policy.ts`
- `packages/node/src/utils/hevy-client-observability.ts`
- `packages/operations/src/workouts.ts`

Endpoint identity and policy are represented by independent lists or branches. A change can therefore drift between client retry behavior, Core read-miss handling, safe diagnostics, operations behavior, and Node metric normalization.

The central model must keep distinct policy facts rather than flattening them into one broad allowlist. Unknown endpoints must remain fail-closed, and diagnostic redaction must not be weakened.

### 2. Shared operations remain shallow

Relevant files:

- `packages/operations/src/workouts.ts`
- `packages/operations/src/index.ts`
- `packages/core/src/tools/*.ts`
- `packages/cli/src/commands/index.ts`

The operations workspace proves the desired seam through `workouts.list`, but most Core tools and CLI commands still orchestrate the curated Hevy client separately. Grow #872 domain by domain; adapters should retain argument parsing, presentation, and runtime observation rather than Hevy-domain workflow policy.

### 3. Validation repeats tests and builds

Relevant files:

- `project.json`
- `nx.json`
- `package.json`
- `repository/validation-lanes.json`
- `tests/package/*`
- `.github/workflows/build-and-test.yml`

Specialized contract, stdio, and CLI tests are all selected by unit and then executed again by their named lanes. The build/pack path also rebuilds Node and CLI artifacts inside package smoke work after earlier graph producers have run.

Disjointness must preserve complete coverage and focused debugging commands. Artifact consumers must reject stale output; this is not permission to remove custom policy checks or package-install smoke behavior.

### 4. Node lifecycle duplication

Relevant files:

- `packages/node/src/index.ts`
- `packages/node/src/utils/graceful-shutdown.ts`
- `packages/node/src/streamable-http.ts`
- `packages/node/src/index.test.ts`

`runStdioServer` and the HTTP runner repeat one substantial lifecycle implementation. A private lifecycle runner with two real transport adapters would improve locality without erasing transport-specific behavior.

### 5. Repeated deterministic test machinery

Relevant files:

- `tests/integration/mocked/hevy-mcp.mocked.integration.test.ts`
- `tests/integration/mocked/get-workout-count-events-mocked.integration.test.ts`
- `packages/core/src/tools/*.test.ts`
- `docs/testing-strategy.md`

This is renewed current-state evidence for #606. A shared test-support module should remain private, fail on leaked sessions/interceptors/network calls, and preserve visible failure diagnostics.

### 6. Response-contract implementation breadth

Relevant files:

- `packages/core/src/utils/response-contracts.ts`
- `packages/core/src/utils/response-contracts.test.ts`

Keep the existing deep public response interface. Explore compiling each validation schema once and organizing private domain implementations around shared pagination behavior. Preserve exact structured schemas and legacy text output.

### 7. Unmeasured Worker admission cost

Relevant files:

- `packages/worker/src/worker.ts`
- `packages/worker/src/worker.test.ts`
- `tests/performance/scenario.ts`
- `tests/performance/performance.test.ts`

The first deliverable is a representative repeated-request benchmark. Any reuse design must explicitly preserve credential revocation, tenant isolation, request isolation, and stateless transport semantics.

### 8. Residual control-plane drift

Relevant files:

- `scripts/control-plane-validation.mjs`
- `scripts/control-plane-models.mjs`
- `scripts/repository-control-plane.mjs`
- `scripts/render-validation-lanes.mjs`
- `repository/validation-lanes.json`
- `project.json`
- `docs/contributor-onboarding.md`
- `docs/testing-strategy.md`

`control-plane-validation.mjs` is 1,091 lines. Twenty-six of 28 mapped lanes repeat the same alias and Nx target name. Validation/rendering code rereads overlapping sources, while handwritten changing facts have drifted.

Derive simple one-to-one projections from one validated model seam. Preserve custom commands, cache exceptions, runtime/package policy, release policy, and the compiler-backed dependency checker as explicit policy.

## Recommended routing order

1. Define the endpoint-policy ownership and coordinate it with #928.
2. Add the measured validation baseline and artifact-flow slice to #882.
3. Decide whether to reopen #606 or file a narrowed successor.
4. Continue shared operations through #872 and Node lifecycle through #878.
5. File a focused response-contract implementation/benchmark issue if accepted.
6. Add the Worker benchmark requirement to #879 before any reuse design.
7. Route residual control-plane and documentation drift to #882 or a focused successor.

This is an ordering for maintainer leverage, not a requirement to combine the work into one branch or pull request.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Every finding above is marked accepted, deferred, or rejected with a short rationale.
- [ ] Every accepted finding has exactly one owning issue; existing issues are reused where their scope already matches.
- [ ] The endpoint-policy owner distinguishes retry, expected-absence, diagnostic-safety, and metric-identity facts and remains fail-closed for unknown endpoints.
- [ ] #882 records the cold/warm baseline and requires before/after execution counts and wall time without weakening validation.
- [ ] #606 is either reopened, replaced by a narrower issue, or remains closed with a current rationale that addresses the repeated setup still present.
- [ ] Response-contract work is preceded by an allocation/render benchmark and preserves externally visible contracts.
- [ ] #879 receives a repeated-request Worker benchmark before any validation or server reuse is approved.
- [ ] Residual control-plane/docs drift has an owner and generated/parity-checked projections replace only derivable duplication.
- [ ] Accepted runtime/package changes identify their Changeset cascade from `repository/topology.json`.
- [ ] No accepted item requires editing `packages/hevy-client/src/generated/` by hand.

## Guardrails

- Preserve runtime-neutral direction: `hevy-client → operations → core`, with Node, Worker, and CLI as independent adapters.
- Keep generated client internals private and regenerated from their source.
- Keep npm scripts as compatibility entrypoints while Nx owns graph/input/output/cache metadata.
- Preserve the custom compiler-backed package-policy check; generic tooling may complement but not silently replace it.
- Do not broaden safe diagnostic data while deduplicating endpoint/error policy.
- Do not add Worker credential caching or shared mutable state without revocation and isolation evidence.
- Do not turn this tracking issue into one large implementation pull request.

## Validation expectations

Each implementation issue should run the focused lane for its changed seam plus the repository baseline:

```text
mise exec -- npm run check
mise exec -- npm run check:types
mise exec -- npm run build
mise exec -- npm run test:pr
mise exec -- npm run test:performance
mise exec -- npm run check:changeset
```

Performance-oriented work must publish the exact before/after command, cold/warm state, execution count, wall time, and any correctness trade-off.

## Non-goals

- Reopening completed roadmap issues merely to duplicate their accepted scope.
- Creating a second operations, lifecycle, Worker-routing, or validation model beside #872, #878, #879, or #882.
- Removing safety, release, package, privacy, or compatibility checks to improve timing.
- Designing a Worker cache before measuring the actual hot path.
- Splitting cohesive modules only because they are large.

## Review relationship

This is a current-checkout follow-up to the completed synthesis in #865 and portfolio decision in #866. It records what remains observable after subsequent architecture and Nx work, and routes those deltas into the live backlog.

issues.title: Consolidate Node lifecycle and bound HTTP session capacity
issues.body:
## Outcome

Node stdio and HTTP share one startup/config/telemetry/shutdown lifecycle while HTTP sessions and initialization consume bounded, observable capacity.

## Ownership seam

The Node runtime owns process lifecycle, stdio/HTTP adapters, admission, session state, telemetry providers, and shutdown. Shared operation/outcome behavior stays below it.

## Scope

- Remove duplicated startup paths for config, telemetry, key validation, update checks, failure recording, and shutdown.
- Add session caps, idle expiry, initialization concurrency limits, application body deadlines, and deterministic cleanup.
- Return stable 429/503 recovery guidance for local capacity rejection.
- Cancel active upstream work on disconnect, eviction, and shutdown.
- Contain optional telemetry initialization/export failures so they cannot prevent serving.

## Non-goals

- Merging Node and Worker transports.
- Adding process restart supervision inside the library.
- Weakening host, bearer, body, or session security checks.
- Broad circuit breakers.

## Portfolio placement

Wave 3 — adapter projections and runtime policy

Primary priority: Resiliency

## Dependencies

- [Establish end-to-end execution control and outcome semantics](https://github.com/chrisdoc/hevy-mcp/issues/871)
- [Build the versioned operator contract and doctor interface](https://github.com/chrisdoc/hevy-mcp/issues/877)

## Migration and release policy

Preserve current stdio and HTTP invocation syntax until coordinated cutover. New capacity settings must have safe documented defaults and additive configuration first.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Common lifecycle behavior has one implementation across stdio and HTTP.
- [ ] Capacity, expiry, and initialization limits are deterministic and recover after eviction.
- [ ] Disconnect and shutdown abort active Hevy work within the configured bound.
- [ ] Optional telemetry failure cannot block startup, requests, or cleanup.
- [ ] Existing raw-chunk stdio instrumentation and HTTP security tests remain green.

## Validation

- `npm run test:stdio`
- `npm run test:contract`
- `npm run test:worker-http`
- `npm run build`
- `npx vitest run --exclude tests/integration/**`
- `npm run check`
- `npm run check:types`
- `npm run check:changeset`

## Stopping conditions

- Do not introduce unbounded queues behind the admission limit.
- Stop if common lifecycle extraction erases real stdio/HTTP differences.

## Roadmap source

Portfolio decision: [Choose the improvement portfolio and breaking-change migration policy](https://github.com/chrisdoc/hevy-mcp/issues/866)

Architecture source: [Synthesize deep-module boundaries and cross-cutting opportunities](https://github.com/chrisdoc/hevy-mcp/issues/865#issuecomment-5166093667)

issues.title: Create the shared Hevy operations and capability workspace
issues.body:
## Outcome

MCP and CLI consume one runtime-neutral module for Hevy operation policy and typed capability descriptors instead of independently orchestrating the curated client.

## Ownership seam

A new `@hevy-mcp/operations` workspace owns intent-level reads/writes, normalization, expected absence, pagination, search, composite workflows, cache/degradation policy, mutation semantics, canonical field metadata, and capability identifiers.

## Scope

- Insert `hevy-client → operations → core → node/worker`, with `operations → cli`, while preserving runtime neutrality.
- Move shared orchestration out of MCP tools/workflows and CLI dispatch behind a small typed interface.
- Define canonical operation descriptors for intent, input/output, safety, field mappings, and outcome contract.
- Provide an in-memory Hevy adapter and test behavior through the operations interface.
- Delete superseded duplicated policy and tests once equivalent interface-level coverage exists.

## Non-goals

- A generic stringly operation dispatcher.
- Merging MCP schemas with generated Hevy schemas.
- Owning CLI rendering, MCP registration, transports, or runtime lifecycle.
- Exposing generated Kubb internals as public package API.

## Portfolio placement

Wave 2 — deep foundations

Primary priority: Maintainer leverage

## Dependencies

- [Establish end-to-end execution control and outcome semantics](https://github.com/chrisdoc/hevy-mcp/issues/871)

## Migration and release policy

Internal architecture may break private imports, but public MCP/CLI behavior must remain compatible until the coordinated major cutover. Add an empty Changeset when no runtime behavior changes.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] MCP and CLI execute shared operations through the new interface.
- [ ] Pagination, absence, mutation replacement/patch rules, search, and composite workflows each have one implementation owner.
- [ ] The workspace passes package-boundary, export, bundle, and Changeset propagation checks.
- [ ] Interface-level tests replace duplicated implementation tests without reducing behavioral coverage.
- [ ] Deleting the module would demonstrably redistribute policy across both adapters.

## Validation

- `npm run check:workspaces`
- `npm run check:boundaries`
- `npm run check:exports`
- `npm run build:packages`
- `npx vitest run --exclude tests/integration/**`
- `npm run check`
- `npm run check:types`
- `npm run check:changeset`

## Stopping conditions

- Do not expose a broad interface mirroring every generated client method without hiding policy.
- Stop if Node built-ins or Worker-specific globals enter the runtime-neutral workspace.

## Roadmap source

Portfolio decision: [Choose the improvement portfolio and breaking-change migration policy](https://github.com/chrisdoc/hevy-mcp/issues/866)

Architecture source: [Synthesize deep-module boundaries and cross-cutting opportunities](https://github.com/chrisdoc/hevy-mcp/issues/865#issuecomment-5166093667)

issues.title: Serve dual-era MCP protocols through one primitive factory
issues.body:
## Outcome

One primitive/capability factory serves the 2025 interoperability floor and the 2026 protocol through SDK-supported handlers across Node and Worker without duplicate tool definitions.

## Ownership seam

The protocol-serving module owns protocol-era negotiation, discovery/metadata, standard headers, cache hints, and legacy logging quarantine. Node stdio, Node HTTP, and Worker HTTP remain concrete adapters.

## Scope

- Adopt the SDK modern handler/factory for 2026 requests with documented 2025 fallback.
- Support modern discovery, per-request metadata, standard `Mcp-Method`/`Mcp-Name` headers, and cache hints.
- Keep stateful Node HTTP legacy behavior isolated from stateless Worker requests.
- Use the current SDK stdio serving path without losing required raw-chunk observability.
- Confine deprecated MCP logging to the legacy adapter.

## Non-goals

- Removing 2025 support in the next major.
- Merging Node and Worker transport implementations.
- Adopting Tasks, sampling, roots, legacy SSE, or universal progress.
- Reimplementing SDK protocol logic.

## Portfolio placement

Wave 3 — adapter projections and runtime policy

Primary priority: Resiliency and interoperability

## Dependencies

- [Create the shared Hevy operations and capability workspace](https://github.com/chrisdoc/hevy-mcp/issues/872)
- [Project MCP contracts from canonical capability descriptors](https://github.com/chrisdoc/hevy-mcp/issues/874)

## Migration and release policy

Dual-era support is mandatory throughout the next major because the 2026 protocol is new. Removal may occur only in a later major after conformance and supported-client evidence.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The same primitive registry serves both protocol eras.
- [ ] Existing 2025 clients retain current behavior and tests.
- [ ] Modern clients receive discovery, request metadata, standard headers, and stateless semantics where applicable.
- [ ] Protocol-era logic does not leak into operation implementations.
- [ ] The stdio observability suite passes after the SDK serving change.

## Validation

- `npm run test:contract`
- `npm run test:stdio`
- `npm run test:worker`
- `npm run test:worker-http`
- `npm run build`
- `npx vitest run --exclude tests/integration/**`
- `npm run check`
- `npm run check:types`
- `npm run check:changeset`

## Stopping conditions

- Do not remove the legacy era based only on SDK availability.
- Stop if modern serving requires copying SDK internals instead of using supported interfaces.

## Roadmap source

Portfolio decision: [Choose the improvement portfolio and breaking-change migration policy](https://github.com/chrisdoc/hevy-mcp/issues/866)

Architecture source: [Synthesize deep-module boundaries and cross-cutting opportunities](https://github.com/chrisdoc/hevy-mcp/issues/865#issuecomment-5166093667)

issues.title: Build the versioned operator contract and doctor interface
issues.body:
## Outcome

Operators can discover, configure, authenticate, verify, diagnose, upgrade, recover, and remove every supported surface through one versioned product contract and privacy-safe doctor/preflight interface.

## Ownership seam

An operator-experience module owns product surfaces, version requirements, config/auth/readiness lifecycle, diagnostic checks, migration/recovery actions, and human/JSON projections.

## Scope

- Define supported hosted, Node stdio/HTTP, Docker, self-hosted Worker, and CLI surfaces with canonical endpoints and auth modes.
- Define typed configuration names, defaults, precedence, redaction, and invalid-value behavior.
- Implement doctor/preflight checks for runtime/package, config, DNS/reachability/auth, transport/bind policy, OAuth discovery, and applicable Worker bindings.
- Support stable human and JSON output, documented exit codes, `--no-network`, correlation IDs, and copyable remediation.
- Expose safe readiness/version facts that distinguish configured, alive, transport-ready, Hevy-reachable, and credential-valid states.

## Non-goals

- Duplicating capability or repository topology models.
- Exposing secrets or raw errors.
- Treating deployment command success as readiness.
- Making maintainer-owned telemetry mandatory for self-hosters.

## Portfolio placement

Wave 3 — adapter projections and runtime policy

Primary priority: Human operator ergonomics

## Dependencies

- [Establish end-to-end execution control and outcome semantics](https://github.com/chrisdoc/hevy-mcp/issues/871)

## Migration and release policy

Add doctor/config inspection and readiness surfaces incrementally. Configuration normalization may remove aliases only at the coordinated major cutover.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Every supported surface and auth path appears once in the product model.
- [ ] Doctor runs safely with missing, invalid, and valid credentials and preserves unknown versus failed.
- [ ] Node and CLI emit actionable parse/config diagnostics and stable JSON errors.
- [ ] Hosted identity, running version, auth modes, and readiness are safely inspectable.
- [ ] Diagnostic fixtures prove complete redaction and remediation accuracy.

## Validation

- `npm run test:contract`
- `npm run test:stdio`
- `npm run test:worker`
- `npm run test:worker-http`
- `npm run test:cli`
- `npm run build`
- `npx vitest run --exclude tests/integration/**`
- `npm run check`
- `npm run check:types`
- `npm run check:changeset`

## Stopping conditions

- Do not make live Hevy reachability a prerequisite for metadata-only readiness.
- Stop if diagnostic output cannot be proven secret-free.

## Roadmap source

Portfolio decision: [Choose the improvement portfolio and breaking-change migration policy](https://github.com/chrisdoc/hevy-mcp/issues/866)

Architecture source: [Synthesize deep-module boundaries and cross-cutting opportunities](https://github.com/chrisdoc/hevy-mcp/issues/865#issuecomment-5166093667)

issues.title: refactor: remove verified dead code, stale docs, and duplicate validation work
issues.body:
## Outcome

Remove code, documentation, dependencies, and repeated validation work that have a verified surviving owner, while preserving runtime behavior, focused test interfaces, generated output, safety policy, and release guarantees.

This is the focused deletion successor to #937. It should not absorb the broader architecture roadmap, the custom-script reduction owned by #911, or the full validation redesign owned by #882.

## Review baseline

- Snapshot: `origin/main` at `2443cad60f74c21ec38592d2083e7fac1398401a`.
- Review mode: read-only; the source checkout and dedicated review worktree remained clean.
- Static checks: repository-wide symbol/reference search, dependency graph inspection, `npm explain`, and Vitest discovery comparison.
- Unit discovery: 76 files / 842 tests.
- Contract, stdio, and CLI lanes repeat 12 unit-selected files / 117 unique unit-selected test cases in the local PR aggregate.

## HTML review

- [Open the GitHub-hosted HTML report](https://gist.github.com/chrisdoc/1fedb609ba913ed3976555389e4a078d)
- [Download the raw HTML report](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/chrisdoc/1fedb609ba913ed3976555389e4a078d/raw/84722c79065c97f0ed254f5470212d6cf7dd89a6/architecture-review-20260807-204439.html)

The uploaded file is `architecture-review-20260807-204439.html` (19,219 bytes). Its downloaded SHA-256 matches the reviewed local file: `2fb830560e4e5f54b51209ad1f66834e3d3a607241848f157644e496e4b98c49`.

## Phase 1: verified removals

Implement these as small package- or concern-focused pull requests, not one broad cleanup branch.

### 1. Delete forwarding modules and orphaned runtime declarations

- [ ] Delete `packages/core/src/utils/safe-error-diagnostic.ts`; retarget internal imports to the surviving implementation in `packages/core/src/utils/error-policy.ts`.
- [ ] Delete `packages/node/src/utils/result-telemetry.ts`; retarget its two Node consumers to the surviving Core implementation.
- [ ] Delete `workoutCountResponse` and `workoutCountOutputSchema` from `packages/core/src/utils/response-contracts.ts`; the workout-count resource remains the behavior owner.
- [ ] Delete `executionStatus` from `packages/worker/src/execution-response.ts`; `executionOutcome(...).status` already owns the calculation.
- [ ] Delete `isHttpHostAllowed` from `packages/node/src/utils/streamable-http.ts`; the live server uses the private loopback check directly.
- [ ] Delete `destructiveAnnotations` from `packages/core/src/utils/tool-annotations.ts`; the current tool set has no delete tool.
- [ ] Delete `bodyMeasurementFieldsInputSchema` and its now-unused Zod import from `packages/core/src/mutations.ts`.
- [ ] Delete `replaceWorkoutInputShape` from `packages/core/src/tools/input-schemas.ts`.

These removals eliminate about 41 source lines. Repository search found no runtime consumer for the orphaned declarations, and package export maps do not expose the forwarding file paths as supported package subpaths.

### 2. Remove the unused Kubb plugin

- [ ] Remove `@kubb/plugin-faker` from `package.json` and `package-lock.json`.

`packages/hevy-client/kubb.config.ts` configures only the Core, Client, OAS, TypeScript, and Zod plugins. `npm explain` reports the faker plugin only as a root direct dependency with no dependent.

### 3. Delete the stale onboarding duplicate

- [ ] Confirm no external publishing job or project page depends on `docs/contributor-onboarding.md`.
- [ ] Delete `docs/contributor-onboarding.md` (494 lines).

The file has no inbound repository link, duplicates `CONTRIBUTING.md` and `docs/test-lanes.md`, says there are five workspaces instead of six, and references the removed `packages/core/src/utils/response-formatter.ts` path. `CONTRIBUTING.md` and `docs/test-lanes.md` remain the owners.

### 4. Remove repeated test execution while retaining focused lanes

- [ ] In the local `test:pr` aggregate, stop rerunning `test:contract`, `test:stdio`, and `test:cli` after `test:unit` has selected the same files.
- [ ] Keep the focused aliases and standalone CI lanes for targeted debugging and reporting.
- [ ] In the release workflow, remove the explicit CLI test step only after proving `test:release-unit` discovers the same CLI tests.
- [ ] Publish before/after file counts, test counts, cold/warm wall time, and Nx execution counts.

Route this implementation through the disjoint-validation work in #882. #937 already records the current performance baseline.

## Phase 2: explicit compatibility decisions

These are not automatic deletions. Decide their interface or archival status first.

### Private barrel exports

- [ ] Audit downstream source imports before trimming unused exports from `packages/core/src/index.ts` and `packages/hevy-client/src/index.ts`.
- [ ] Remove the unused `ToolResultTelemetry as ToolResultSummary` alias if no downstream source consumer exists.

issues.body:
## Problem Statement

The current observability system is present but not reliably actionable. Operators can see that an MCP session, tool, or process failed, but often cannot determine why, which release introduced the problem, which MCP client experienced it, or whether multiple events represent the same underlying failure.

The current design also spreads telemetry policy across the Node entrypoint, tool observer, SDK observer, API observer, core observation types, tests, and documentation. Each new diagnostic field requires more manual allowlisting and more privacy regression tests. That has created a choice between exporting opaque errors and exporting native exceptions with an unacceptable risk of leaking user data.

Issue #915 documented a concrete example: hundreds of process-failure traces were grouped under generic `McpProcessFailure`/`Error` fields without enough information to distinguish runtime, transport, SDK, and application failures. PR #920 explored moving more of the privacy decision into the Collector, but it changes the data policy before the desired observability contract and introduces raw exception plumbing into the runtime-neutral core.

The current error destination is a self-hosted GlitchTip project. We want to return to Sentry as the error-reporting backend, with proper release tracking, issue grouping, source maps, alerts, and trace correlation. GlitchTip should be removed from the active configuration and documentation.

### Goals

- Make user-visible failures actionable in Sentry.
- Make OTel traces explain what happened before and during a failure.
- Preserve low-cardinality metrics for reliability and performance dashboards.
- Capture sanitized exception messages and stacks without exporting prompts, tool arguments, tool results, credentials, or fitness data.
- Report each logical failure once instead of duplicating it across nested spans and SDK hooks.
- Keep the core package runtime-neutral and free of native exception transport concerns.
- Make the telemetry implementation easier to change by concentrating policy behind a small, deep Node adapter.
- Migrate error reporting from GlitchTip to Sentry SaaS without losing release/source-map diagnostics.

## Solution

Adopt a deliberate two-backend model:

- **Sentry** is the source of truth for actionable errors, crashes, releases, issue grouping, source maps, and error alerts.
- **OpenTelemetry through the Collector to Honeycomb** is the source of truth for traces, latency, retries, sessions, and aggregate metrics.
- **The Collector** performs tail sampling, routing, retention, and final defense-in-depth scrubbing. It is not the only privacy policy enforcement point.

Sentry performance tracing remains disabled. OTel traces remain independent from Sentry, with OTel trace and span identifiers attached to Sentry error events for navigation between systems.

### Failure reporter seam

Introduce one deep Node-only failure-reporting module with a small interface. Callers provide the native error and structured failure context; the module returns an optional correlation/event receipt.

The module will:

1. Classify known error types such as Hevy HTTP, network, validation, protocol, SDK, lifecycle, and process failures.
2. Produce one stable failure record containing bounded taxonomy and operational context.
3. Sanitize the message and stack once, with length, line, path, credential, URL, and nested-cause limits.
4. Send one sanitized exception to Sentry.
5. Attach the same structured fields and a standard exception event to the owning OTel span.
6. Link the Sentry event to the active OTel trace and expose a short diagnostic/correlation ID where appropriate.
7. Treat telemetry failures as best-effort and never alter MCP behavior.

The runtime-neutral core will retain only safe observation data. Native `unknown` exceptions will not be added to the core observation contract. The Node observer already wraps execution and can retain the native error at the Node seam.

### Approved diagnostic data

Capture as structured context:

- service, release, runtime, OS, and architecture;
- MCP transport and sanitized client/protocol metadata;
- fixed tool name, feature, operation, and read/write kind;
- API method, normalized endpoint, status, retry count, timeout phase, and commit state;
- stable error type, category, code, expectedness, and retryability;
- bounded sanitized message and stack for actionable failures;
- OTel trace/span IDs, Sentry event ID, and a per-failure diagnostic ID.

Never capture:

- API keys, bearer tokens, authorization headers, or request bodies;
- prompts, prompt arguments, tool arguments, or tool result text;
- raw Hevy identifiers, exact dates, workout/routine/template content, names, notes, or measurements;
- arbitrary error object properties, complete response bodies, or URLs containing query data;
- a persistent identity derived from the Hevy API key.

Telemetry is enabled by default for the packaged Node runtime. `HEVY_MCP_TELEMETRY=0` disables all project telemetry. Add a separate diagnostic-detail opt-out so users can retain structural metrics/traces while suppressing exception messages and stacks.

### Error ownership

Define one owner for each logical failure:

- Tool exceptions are captured by the Node tool observer.
- API observers supply structured API context; the tool-level reporter owns the user-visible exception.
- Returned MCP errors affect span status and metrics but do not create exception events.
- Expected not-found outcomes affect metrics and traces but do not create Sentry issues.
- SDK/protocol failures are captured by the SDK adapter.
- Startup and process failures are captured once by the lifecycle/process adapter.
- Telemetry exporter failures are not reported as application failures.

Nested spans may still receive status and bounded attributes, but the native exception is recorded only on the owning span.

### Sentry migration

Move the default error destination from GlitchTip to Sentry SaaS:

- Provision/configure the Sentry project, environments, ownership, retention, and alerts.
- Use a packaged public Sentry DSN with a runtime `SENTRY_DSN` override; an empty value disables Sentry export.
- Continue using the Sentry organization, project, and auth token in release CI for private source-map upload.
- Configure explicit Sentry integrations so automatic process handlers do not duplicate the custom failure reporter.
- Use `captureException` once per logical failure rather than generic exception messages for actionable errors.
- Add a centralized `beforeSend` final scrubber.
- Set release, environment, stable fingerprints, bounded tags/contexts, and OTel trace correlation.
- Generate source maps during release builds, upload them privately to Sentry, and keep them out of the published package.
- Remove active GlitchTip configuration, documentation, tests, and default DSN references. Historical changelog entries may remain as historical records.
- Audit and remove the direct Sentry OTel integration dependency if it is no longer needed after the independent OTel design is complete.

### OTel and Collector behavior

Keep OTel responsible for traces and metrics:

- Preserve a clear session/request → MCP tool → Hevy API → retry/cache span hierarchy.
- Use standard span status and exception semantics with the sanitized failure record.
- Keep messages and stacks out of metric attributes.
- Retain all error and slow traces at the Collector, and sample successful traces.
- Keep all low-cardinality metrics, with alerts for exporter drops, stale data, queue pressure, and Collector health.
- Maintain a final Collector scrubber and regression fixtures, but do not rely on the Collector as the sole privacy control.

### Worker alignment

The Worker must not import Node telemetry. After the Node design is proven, add a separate Worker adapter that emits the same failure taxonomy and correlation fields through the Worker’s supported logging/error facilities. A Worker-side OTel SDK is not part of the first implementation slice.

## Commits

Each commit below must leave the repository buildable and tests runnable. Runtime/package commits require the appropriate non-empty Changeset before committing, and the Changeset status check must pass before each commit that is prepared for review.

1. **`docs: define observability goals and data contract`**
   - Record the two-backend responsibility split, approved diagnostic fields, prohibited data, retention assumptions, and the Sentry migration decision.
   - Define the failure taxonomy, expected-error policy, and ownership matrix.

2. **`test: add representative failure and redaction fixtures`**
   - Add fixtures for Hevy HTTP errors, network errors, validation errors, SDK errors, process failures, malformed thrown values, nested causes, credentials, local paths, and response-body sentinels.
   - Establish tests against externally visible normalized records rather than private helper implementation details.

3. **`refactor: introduce the centralized failure record normalizer`**
   - Implement the single classifier/scrubber that produces bounded operational fields and sanitized diagnostic details.
   - Keep native error objects inside the Node package.
   - Verify stable behavior for expected errors and unknown thrown values.

4. **`refactor: add the Node failure reporter seam`**
   - Add the small reporter interface and adapters for Sentry and OTel.
   - Add correlation/event receipt handling.
   - Preserve best-effort behavior and make provider failures invisible to MCP callers.

5. **`refactor: route lifecycle and process failures through the reporter`**
   - Replace scattered lifecycle exception attribute construction with structured failure contexts.
   - Ensure startup, connect, runtime, uncaught-exception, and unhandled-rejection failures are captured once.
   - Preserve Node’s normal termination semantics.

6. **`refactor: route tool failures through one owner`**
   - Let the Node tool observer retain and report native tool exceptions at its execution seam.
   - Keep the core completion observation safe and runtime-neutral.
   - Stop the SDK wrapper and nested spans from emitting duplicate native exception events.

7. **`refactor: remove obsolete raw-exception plumbing and duplicated policy`**
   - Remove the proposed native exception field from the core observation contract if present.
   - Delete per-call privacy allowlist spreading and obsolete generic exception adapters.
   - Keep only one source of truth for failure context construction.

8. **`feat: restore Sentry SaaS as the error backend`**
   - Replace the GlitchTip default destination with the packaged Sentry DSN and runtime override behavior.
   - Configure explicit integrations, release/environment metadata, stable fingerprints, `beforeSend` scrubbing, and OTel trace correlation.
   - Update provider mocks and tests for one-event capture and duplicate-handler prevention.

9. **`build: upload private Sentry release artifacts`**
   - Make release builds generate and upload source maps to Sentry without including them in the npm package.
   - Add a release smoke test that verifies readable mapped stack frames and release attribution.

10. **`feat: align OTel span exception and sampling behavior`**
    - Record sanitized standard exception events only on owning spans.
    - Normalize span names and semantic attributes.
    - Add slow/error trace sampling rules and preserve all low-cardinality metrics.

11. **`chore: remove GlitchTip configuration and documentation`**
    - Remove active GlitchTip references, default DSN fixtures, destination assumptions, and obsolete environment descriptions.
    - Leave historical changelog records untouched.
    - Audit dependencies and remove direct packages that are no longer used.

12. **`feat: add observability dashboards and incident runbook`**
    - Migrate error views and alerts from GlitchTip to Sentry.
    - Add release, tool, client, API-status, startup, latency, and trace-correlation views.
    - Document the operator workflow from a Sentry issue to its Honeycomb trace.

13. **`test: verify end-to-end telemetry payloads`**
    - Exercise the actual Sentry event normalization hook and serialized OTel exporter payloads.
    - Verify secret/path/body/prompt absence, one-event ownership, release metadata, source-map attribution, Collector redaction, and exporter-failure resilience.

14. **`feat: align Worker failure diagnostics`**
    - Implement the same stable taxonomy and bounded correlation fields using Worker-supported facilities.
    - Keep this adapter independent from Node packages and defer Worker OTel SDK adoption unless a separate decision approves it.

15. **`refactor: remove superseded telemetry implementation`**
    - Delete dead helpers, stale tests, obsolete documentation, and compatibility paths only after the new behavior has been observed in a controlled release.

## Decision Document

- Sentry SaaS is the error-reporting backend. GlitchTip is removed from active runtime configuration.
- Honeycomb through the OTel Collector remains the trace and metric backend.
- Sentry performance tracing is disabled; OTel tracing is independent.
- Sentry receives one sanitized exception per logical actionable failure.
- OTel receives one sanitized exception event on the owning span plus structured span status/attributes.
- The Collector is a final safety and routing layer, not the only privacy enforcement layer.
- Error messages and stacks are allowed only after centralized bounded scrubbing.
- Prompts, arguments, results, credentials, raw IDs, exact dates, response bodies, and arbitrary object fields remain prohibited.
- No API-key-derived user hash or persistent user behavior identity is introduced.
- A per-failure diagnostic/correlation ID is preferred over persistent user tracking.
- The Node core interface remains runtime-neutral and does not transport native exceptions.
- Sentry’s automatic process-level handlers must not compete with the custom failure reporter.
- Expected not-found and ordinary user/configuration failures should not create noisy Sentry issues; they remain queryable through OTel metrics and traces.
- Public Sentry DSN configuration may be packaged; Sentry auth tokens and release credentials remain CI secrets.
- Source maps are uploaded privately to Sentry and excluded from the public package.
- The first implementation focuses on Node. Worker parity follows after the Node contract is validated.

## Testing Decisions

Good tests will verify externally visible telemetry behavior: what is sent, where it is sent, how it is grouped, whether it correlates to a trace, and whether MCP behavior remains unchanged. Tests should not assert incidental helper structure or the exact number of internal function calls unless that number is part of the duplicate-event contract.

Test coverage will include:

- deterministic normalization of each known error family;
- bounded messages, stacks, causes, paths, codes, statuses, and endpoints;
- removal of credentials, headers, prompts, arguments, results, bodies, and raw identifiers;
- expected-error suppression from Sentry;
- one logical failure producing one Sentry event and one owning OTel exception event;
- OTel trace/span ID and Sentry event ID correlation;
- explicit Sentry integration configuration and absence of duplicate process handlers;
- Sentry release/environment/fingerprint behavior;
- private source-map upload and mapped release stacks;
- actual serialized OTLP spans rather than only mocked `recordException` calls;
- Collector redaction and tail-sampling fixtures;
- provider/network failures not affecting MCP responses, process termination, or shutdown;
- telemetry opt-out and diagnostic-detail opt-out behavior;
- Node/Worker package boundary rules;
- dashboard query smoke checks and telemetry freshness.

Validation for the implementation will include the repository build, formatting/lint checks, type checks, unit tests, focused Node stdio observability tests, release-build tests, and the required Changeset status check.

## Out of Scope

- Exporting raw prompts, tool arguments, tool results, API keys, authorization headers, full request/response bodies, or raw fitness data.
- Adding persistent user-level behavior tracking or deriving a user identity from the Hevy API key.
- Migrating Honeycomb, ClickHouse, or the OTel Collector to another vendor.
- Enabling Sentry performance tracing or adding a Sentry span processor to the OTel provider.
- Adding a Worker-side OTel SDK in the initial Node migration.
- Changing MCP response contracts or exposing internal stack traces to MCP clients.
- Rewriting historical changelog entries that mention GlitchTip.
- Building a general-purpose logging framework.

## Further Notes

- This issue supersedes the narrow diagnostic approach in #915 and should be treated as the architectural follow-up to PR #920.
- Before implementation begins, operators should inspect a representative sample of current Sentry/GlitchTip events and OTel traces, including the 578 process failures referenced by #915, to establish a baseline for noise, duplication, and missing context.
- Success means an operator can open a Sentry issue and answer: which release failed, which MCP client and tool were involved, what stable error/API condition occurred, whether the issue is new or regressed, and which Honeycomb trace shows the failure path.
- The migration should be released in a controlled canary first. Compare event volume, duplicate rate, mapped-stack coverage, trace correlation, and sensitive-field regression results before removing the old compatibility paths.

issues.title: Apply one validation model to CI, artifacts, coverage, and releases
issues.body:
## Outcome

Local, pull-request, release, and deployment workflows consume one validation-lane model, test every public candidate artifact, and enforce honest coverage/release semantics without duplicated execution.

## Ownership seam

Safety-net consumers own workflow orchestration, reporters, credentials, artifact gates, coverage aggregation, and release/deployment policy. Stable lane facts come from the repository control plane.

## Scope

- Make aggregate lanes disjoint while retaining focused debug commands and intentional runtime diversity.
- Define and baseline the production coverage denominator; merge reports deterministically and add behavior-specific ratchets.
- Gate Node and CLI tarballs, Docker image, and Worker candidate artifacts before publication/deployment.
- Add structured release simulations for Node-only, CLI-only, Worker-only, mixed, release-PR, and publish cases.
- Separate deterministic artifact gates from retried live canaries with explicit health, rollback, and manual-override policy.
- Record execution count and wall-time before and after without weakening correctness.

## Non-goals

- Inventing a global coverage percentage before measuring the denominator.
- Making transient Hevy availability block package publication.
- Removing SHA pinning or security scans.
- Change-impact optimization before lane parity.

## Portfolio placement

Wave 4 — proof and enforcement

Primary priority: Maintainer leverage

## Dependencies

- [Repair generated-client output closure and enforce regeneration drift](https://github.com/chrisdoc/hevy-mcp/issues/870)
- [Centralize repository topology, artifact provenance, and validation lanes](https://github.com/chrisdoc/hevy-mcp/issues/873)
- [Generate the complete MCP contract matrix and conformance lane](https://github.com/chrisdoc/hevy-mcp/issues/880)

## Migration and release policy

Internal CI/workflow changes may break private composition. Preserve documented command aliases for one release cycle. Use an empty Changeset.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Local `test:pr`, pull-request CI, and release consume identical lane identities.
- [ ] Every public artifact is tested as the exact candidate that would ship.
- [ ] Coverage excludes/labels generated, type-only, and entrypoint files deliberately and enforces reviewed ratchets.
- [ ] Release simulations catch missing packages, wrong cascades, permissions/provenance errors, and failed canary/rollback paths.
- [ ] Duplicate builds/tests and Worker dry-runs are removed with measured savings.

## Validation

- `npm run test:pr`
- `npm run test:coverage`
- `npm run test:pack`
- `npm run test:pack:cli`
- `npm run worker:dry-run`
- `npm run check:release-candidates`
- `npm run check:package-changesets`
- `npm run check`
- `npm run check:types`
- `npm run check:changeset`

## Stopping conditions

- Do not lower existing gates to achieve disjointness.
- Stop if a live canary becomes the only proof that a deterministic candidate artifact is valid.

## Roadmap source

Portfolio decision: [Choose the improvement portfolio and breaking-change migration policy](https://github.com/chrisdoc/hevy-mcp/issues/866)

Architecture source: [Synthesize deep-module boundaries and cross-cutting opportunities](https://github.com/chrisdoc/hevy-mcp/issues/865#issuecomment-5166093667)
