+import { readFile, stat } from "node:fs/promises";
+import { dirname, resolve } from "node:path";
+import { fileURLToPath } from "node:url";
+
+export const repositoryRoot = resolve(
+	dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)),
+	"..",
+);
+
+export function candidateTarballFilename({ name, version }) {
+	if (typeof name !== "string" || !name) {
+		throw new Error("Release candidate package name is required");
+	}
+	if (typeof version !== "string" || !version) {
+		throw new Error(`Release candidate version is required for ${name}`);
+	}
+	return `${name.replace(/^@/, "").replaceAll("/", "-")}-${version}.tgz`;
+}
+
+export async function releaseCandidateArtifact(
+	packageDirectory,
+	{ repositoryRoot: root = repositoryRoot } = {},
+) {
+	const manifestPath = resolve(root, packageDirectory, "package.json");
+	const manifest = JSON.parse(await readFile(manifestPath, "utf8"));
+	const filename = candidateTarballFilename(manifest);
+	const path = resolve(root, ".nx/pack", filename);
+	let details = null;
+	try {
+		details = await stat(path);
+	} catch (error) {
+		if (
+			!error ||
+			typeof error !== "object" ||
+			!("code" in error) ||
+			error.code !== "ENOENT"
+		) {
+			throw error;
+		}
+	}
+	if (!details?.isFile() || details.size === 0) {
+		throw new Error(
+			`Release candidate is missing or empty for ${manifest.name}@${manifest.version}: ${path}`,
+		);
+	}
+	return {
+		name: manifest.name,
+		version: manifest.version,
+		manifest,
+		filename,
+		path,
+		size: details.size,
+	};
+}

## Reviewer's Guide Accelerates CI by orchestrating Node build, package smoke, Publint, and performance checks around shared prebuilt tarballs, consolidating validation into Nx run-many graphs per Node runtime, tightening workflow projection validation, and introducing CI-specific reporting and Docker cache reuse. #### Flow diagram for shared release candidate artifacts in CI ```mermaid flowchart TD NodeBuild[nx run repository:build] PackArtifacts[pack:artifacts\npack-release-candidates.mjs] Tarballs[.nx/pack\nNode & CLI tarballs] TestPack[test:pack\nnpm-pack-smoke.mjs] TestPackCli[test:pack:cli\ncli npm-pack-smoke.mjs] CheckPublint[check:publint\ncheck-candidate-publint.mjs] TestPerformance[test:performance\nvitest performance.test.ts] NodeBuild --> PackArtifacts PackArtifacts --> Tarballs Tarballs --> TestPack Tarballs --> TestPackCli Tarballs --> CheckPublint NodeBuild --> TestPerformance ``` #### Flow diagram for Nx workflow projection parsing of run-many commands ```mermaid flowchart TD WorkflowStep[GitHub Actions step.run] ParseExecutions[parseWorkflowLaneExecutions] ParseCommands[parseNxRunCommands] OptionValue[optionValue] LaneTargets[mappedLaneTargets] LaneExecutions[Lane execution entries] WorkflowStep --> ParseExecutions ParseExecutions --> ParseCommands ParseCommands --> OptionValue ParseExecutions --> LaneTargets ParseExecutions --> LaneExecutions ``` ### File-Level Changes | Change | Details | Files | | ------ | ------- | ----- | | Consolidate CI validation into Nx run-many graphs per Node runtime while preserving Node 24/26 lane semantics and CI reporting behavior. |
  • Replace many individual npx nx run steps in build-and-test.yml with two Nx run-many aggregates for Node 24 and Node 26, with bounded parallelism.
  • Add HEVY_TEST_REPORT_MODE-based CI reporting via scripts/run-vitest-lane.mjs and wire unit/mocked lanes to use it.
  • Update docs (test-lanes.md, testing-strategy.md, CONTRIBUTING.md, nx-dependency-cruiser-spike.md) and control-plane tests to reflect new aggregates and reporting semantics.

Tips and commands #### Interacting with Sourcery - **Trigger a new review:** Comment `@sourcery-ai review` on the pull request. - **Continue discussions:** Reply directly to Sourcery's review comments. - **Generate a GitHub issue from a review comment:** Ask Sourcery to create an issue from a review comment by replying to it. You can also reply to a review comment with `@sourcery-ai issue` to create an issue from it. - **Generate a pull request title:** Write `@sourcery-ai` anywhere in the pull request title to generate a title at any time. You can also comment `@sourcery-ai title` on the pull request to (re-)generate the title at any time. - **Generate a pull request summary:** Write `@sourcery-ai summary` anywhere in the pull request body to generate a PR summary at any time exactly where you want it. You can also comment `@sourcery-ai summary` on the pull request to (re-)generate the summary at any time. - **Generate reviewer's guide:** Comment `@sourcery-ai guide` on the pull request to (re-)generate the reviewer's guide at any time. - **Resolve all Sourcery comments:** Comment `@sourcery-ai resolve` on the pull request to resolve all Sourcery comments. Useful if you've already addressed all the comments and don't want to see them anymore. - **Dismiss all Sourcery reviews:** Comment `@sourcery-ai dismiss` on the pull request to dismiss all existing Sourcery reviews. comments.body: 💡 Quality: Node 26 test:unit coverage writes outside declared Nx outputs In CI mode the `unit` lane always appends `--coverage` but only adds `--coverage.reportsDirectory=coverage/unit` when the runtime is Node 24. On the Node 26 validation graph (which sets HEVY_TEST_REPORT_MODE=ci and runs test:unit), coverage is therefore written to Vitest's default `./coverage` rather than the `coverage/unit`/`test-results/unit-tests.xml` paths declared in the cacheable `test:unit` target's `outputs`. Nx will report missing outputs and cache an incomplete artifact for that runtime. Impact is low (Node 26 does not upload coverage), but consider pointing the Node 26 run at `coverage/unit` too, or narrowing the target's declared outputs per runtime. Was this helpful? ✅ Quality: Node 26 test:unit coverage writes outside declared Nx outputs

📄 scripts/run-vitest-lane.mjs:22-36 📄 project.json:64-69
In CI mode the unit lane always appends --coverage but only adds --coverage.reportsDirectory=coverage/unit when the runtime is Node 24. On the Node 26 validation graph (which sets HEVY_TEST_REPORT_MODE=ci and runs test:unit), coverage is therefore written to Vitest's default ./coverage rather than the coverage/unit/test-results/unit-tests.xml paths declared in the cacheable test:unit target's outputs. Nx will report missing outputs and cache an incomplete artifact for that runtime. Impact is low (Node 26 does not upload coverage), but consider pointing the Node 26 run at coverage/unit too, or narrowing the target's declared outputs per runtime.

+import { spawnSync } from "node:child_process";

+
+import {
+	releaseCandidateArtifact,
+	repositoryRoot,
+} from "./release-candidate-artifacts.mjs";

+const publint = resolve(
+	repositoryRoot,
+	"node_modules/.bin",
+	process.platform === "win32" ? "publint.cmd" : "publint",
+);
+const candidates = await Promise.all([
+	releaseCandidateArtifact("packages/node"),
+	releaseCandidateArtifact("packages/cli"),
+]);
+
+for (const candidate of candidates) {
+	const result = spawnSync(
+		publint,
+		["run", "--strict", "--pack=false", candidate.path],
+		{ cwd: repositoryRoot, env: process.env, stdio: "inherit" },
+	);
+	if (result.error) throw result.error;
+	if (result.status !== 0) {
+		throw new Error(
+			`Publint failed for ${candidate.filename} with ${result.signal ? `signal ${result.signal}` : `exit code ${result.status ?? 1}`}`,
+		);
+	}

+import { readFile, stat } from "node:fs/promises";
+import { dirname, resolve } from "node:path";
+import { fileURLToPath } from "node:url";
+
+export const repositoryRoot = resolve(
+	dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)),
+	"..",
+);
+
+export function candidateTarballFilename({ name, version }) {
+	if (typeof name !== "string" || !name) {
+		throw new Error("Release candidate package name is required");
+	}
+	if (typeof version !== "string" || !version) {
+		throw new Error(`Release candidate version is required for ${name}`);
+	}
+	return `${name.replace(/^@/, "").replaceAll("/", "-")}-${version}.tgz`;
+}
+
+export async function releaseCandidateArtifact(
+	packageDirectory,
+	{ repositoryRoot: root = repositoryRoot } = {},
+) {
+	const manifestPath = resolve(root, packageDirectory, "package.json");
+	const manifest = JSON.parse(await readFile(manifestPath, "utf8"));
+	const filename = candidateTarballFilename(manifest);
+	const path = resolve(root, ".nx/pack", filename);
+	let details = null;
+	try {
+		details = await stat(path);
+	} catch (error) {
+		if (
+			!error ||
+			typeof error !== "object" ||
+			!("code" in error) ||
+			error.code !== "ENOENT"
+		) {
+			throw error;
+		}
+	}
+	if (!details?.isFile() || details.size === 0) {
+		throw new Error(
+			`Release candidate is missing or empty for ${manifest.name}@${manifest.version}: ${path}`,
+		);
+	}
+	return {
+		name: manifest.name,
+		version: manifest.version,
+		manifest,
+		filename,
+		path,
+		size: details.size,
+	};
+}

ECMAScript 6 allows programmers to create strings containing variable or expressions using template literals, instead of string concatenation, by writing expressions like `${variable}` between two backtick quotes (`). comments.body: 💡 Quality: Node 26 test:unit coverage writes outside declared Nx outputs In CI mode the `unit` lane always appends `--coverage` but only adds `--coverage.reportsDirectory=coverage/unit` when the runtime is Node 24. On the Node 26 validation graph (which sets HEVY_TEST_REPORT_MODE=ci and runs test:unit), coverage is therefore written to Vitest's default `./coverage` rather than the `coverage/unit`/`test-results/unit-tests.xml` paths declared in the cacheable `test:unit` target's `outputs`. Nx will report missing outputs and cache an incomplete artifact for that runtime. Impact is low (Node 26 does not upload coverage), but consider pointing the Node 26 run at `coverage/unit` too, or narrowing the target's declared outputs per runtime. Was this helpful? Unexpected template string expression


ECMAScript 6 allows programmers to create strings containing variable or expressions using template literals, instead of string concatenation, by writing expressions like `${variable}` between two backtick quotes (`). It is easy to use the wrong quotes when wanting to use template literals, by writing `${variable}`, and ending up with the literal value `${variable}` instead of a string containing the value of the templated expressions.

structuredContent.display_title: ci: accelerate build and test workflows

arguments.body:
## What changed

- Run each Node runtime's deterministic validation as one Nx graph with bounded parallelism while preserving the existing Node 24 and Node 26 lane sets.
- Build once per required runtime, prepare one Node and CLI tarball for package validation, and reuse those tarballs for package smoke and Publint checks.
- Reuse the Node build for performance validation and keep the workerd lane machine-exclusive because contention can violate its five-second timeout.
- Preserve Node 24 unit/mocked coverage, JUnit output, and Node 26 unit coverage through an explicit CI report mode.
- Add GitHub Actions cache reuse for the Docker build.
- Teach workflow projection checks to understand repository-scoped `nx run-many` commands and fail closed on project/target drift.

## Why

The workflows invoked Nx once per lane, while package smoke, CLI package smoke, Publint, and performance validation rebuilt artifacts they had already produced. That serialized recoverable work and validated multiple independently generated package candidates.

This is the measured performance tranche of #882 identified by the architecture review in #937. It references those issues without closing them: #882 still owns byte-identical publish handoff, the merged coverage denominator/ratchets, and structured release simulations.

Refs #882
Refs #937

## Impact

Hosted acceptance against the latest five successful `main` Node 24 jobs:

| Measurement | Wall time |
| --- | ---: |
| Main Node 24 median | 138s |
| PR Node 24 | 85s |
| PR package/performance | 70s |
| PR Node 26 | 72s |
| PR Docker (warm cache) | 18s |

Node 24 improvement: **38.4%**, exceeding the 30% target of at most 96.6s.

Cold-cache local `test:pr` timing:

| Measurement | Wall time |
| --- | ---: |
| Baseline | 55.31s |
| Optimized trial 1 | 37.67s |
| Optimized trial 2 | 35.81s |
| Optimized trial 3 | 34.80s |
| Optimized median | 35.81s |

Local median improvement: **35.3%**.

## Validation

- `mise exec -- npm run check`
- `mise exec -- npm run check:types`
- `mise exec -- npm run build`
- `mise exec -- npm run test:pr -- --outputStyle=stream`
- `mise exec -- npm run test:performance`
- `mise exec -- npm run check:changeset`
- Exact Node 24 build, package preparation, and 18-target CI graph simulation with `--excludeTaskDependencies` (passed; no Node rebuild)
- 55 focused control-plane/workflow tests
- Independent Standards and Spec reviews (no blockers)

Hosted run [31246070848](https://github.com/chrisdoc/hevy-mcp/actions/runs/31246070848) passed the 30% target with every Build and Test job green.

## Summary by Sourcery

Consolidate CI build and validation into shared Nx graphs per Node runtime, reusing prebuilt release candidate artifacts and tightening workflow projection checks for run-many commands.

New Features:
- Introduce shared release candidate tarball management, including packing, lookup, and consumption by package smoke tests and Publint validation.
- Add Vitest lane runner script to control unit and mocked coverage and CI reporting via a single environment-driven interface.
- Support repository-scoped Nx run-many parsing in workflow projection tooling to expand aggregate commands into canonical lane executions.

Enhancements:
- Refactor package smoke and CLI pack tests to validate against prebuilt release candidate tarballs instead of rebuilding packages per run.
- Make performance tests depend on and reuse the shared Node build, keeping their work deterministic and aligned with other validation lanes.
- Update Nx targets and scripts so package validation, Publint checks, and release workflows share the same candidate artifacts and release-only build environment.
- Adjust validation lane configuration to keep the workerd lane machine-exclusive while allowing other package-related lanes to run concurrently from immutable artifacts.
- Extend unit and mocked test targets to expose CI report mode via a dedicated environment input, preserving coverage and JUnit outputs in hosted runs.

CI:
- Restructure the build-and-test workflow to run Nx validation graphs per Node runtime with bounded parallelism and shared preparation of package candidates.
- Add GitHub Actions cache reuse for Docker builds and ensure lane projections cover repository-scoped run-many commands.
- Update release workflow to scope secrets to the release build, prepare shared package candidates once, and validate them via an aggregate Nx run-many step.

Documentation:
- Refresh testing and lane documentation to describe shared candidate tarballs, updated performance dependencies, and CI-specific reporting configuration.
- Update validation aggregate tables and Nx spike notes to reflect new lane membership and concurrent consumption of immutable package artifacts.

Tests:
- Expand control-plane and workflow projection tests to cover new orchestrated targets, run-many parsing, CI reporting inputs, and release candidate validation.
- Add unit tests for release candidate artifact resolution and tarball naming to ensure deterministic packaging behavior.

| --- | ---: |
| Baseline | 55.31s |
| Optimized trial 1 | 37.67s |
| Optimized trial 2 | 35.81s |
| Optimized trial 3 | 34.80s |
| Optimized median | 35.81s |

## Validation

- `mise exec -- npm run check`
- `mise exec -- npm run check:types`
- `mise exec -- npm run build`
- `mise exec -- npm run test:pr -- --outputStyle=stream`
- `mise exec -- npm run test:performance`
- `mise exec -- npm run check:changeset`
- Exact Node 24 build, package preparation, and 18-target CI graph simulation with `--excludeTaskDependencies` (passed; no Node rebuild)
- 55 focused control-plane/workflow tests
- Independent Standards and Spec reviews (no blockers)

## Summary by Sourcery

Consolidate CI build and validation into shared Nx graphs per Node runtime, reusing prebuilt release candidate artifacts and tightening workflow projection checks for run-many commands.

New Features:

- Add Vitest lane runner script to control unit and mocked coverage and CI reporting via a single environment-driven interface.

- Update validation aggregate tables and Nx spike notes to reflect new lane membership and concurrent consumption of immutable package artifacts.

issue.title: refactor: track architecture review findings across runtime and tooling
issue.body:
## Outcome

Turn the 2026-08-07 architecture review into owned implementation work without duplicating the existing roadmap. Each finding should either be routed to an existing issue, receive a focused successor issue, or be explicitly deferred with evidence.

The desired end state is less cross-module policy duplication, shorter validation feedback, deeper runtime-neutral operations, simpler runtime/test internals, and a more navigable repository control plane.

## Review baseline

- Repository snapshot: `origin/main` at `2443cad60f74c21ec38592d2083e7fac1398401a`.
- Exact local PR lane: `mise exec -- npm run test:pr -- --outputStyle=stream`.
- Cold run: **62.1s**; warm run: **33.0s**.
- The cold Nx report attributed **33.8s / 55%** to recoverable work; the warm report still attributed **13.8s / 43%**.
- `test:unit` selected 76 files / 842 tests. The contract, stdio, and CLI lanes added 13 file executions whose files were already selected by unit.
- The review was read-only: the source checkout and dedicated review worktree remained clean.

## Findings and current ownership

| # | Finding | Strength | Current owner / review delta |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | One runtime-neutral endpoint policy module | **Strong — top recommendation** | Adjacent to #928, but not owned there as a cross-runtime source for retry semantics, expected 404s, safe diagnostics, and metric endpoint identity. Keep #928 responsible for failure reporting and telemetry ownership. |
| 2 | Complete the shared Hevy operations module | **Strong** | Continue #872. The workspace currently shares `workouts.list`; Core and CLI still independently implement other pagination, read, mutation, search, and aggregation workflows. |
| 3 | Make PR validation artifact-aware and disjoint | **Strong** | Continue #882 with the measured baseline above. Unit overlaps focused lanes, and package/performance paths rebuild artifacts already produced earlier in the graph. |
| 4 | Collapse Node lifecycle into one runner | **Strong** | Continue #878. The stdio and HTTP paths still repeat process tracking, cancellation, config, run spans, update scheduling, shutdown, telemetry flush, and failure classification. |
| 5 | Deepen deterministic MCP test support | **Strong** | Reassess #606, which is closed as `not_planned`. The two mocked integration suites still repeat server/client/runtime registration, in-memory transport, network isolation, and teardown; Core tool tests also repeat registration/handler discovery. |
| 6 | Compile and partition response contracts | **Worth exploring** | No direct issue found; #874 is adjacent but owns public MCP contract projection, not this private implementation. `response-contracts.ts` is 1,252 lines, constructs a Zod object during each render, and repeats pagination mechanics. Benchmark before claiming material runtime gain. |
| 7 | Measure Worker request admission before caching | **Speculative** | Continue #879. Every Worker POST currently performs an upstream `/v1/user/info` validation and creates/connects a new server and transport. Add a repeated-request Worker benchmark before considering any bounded reuse. |
| 8 | Deepen the repository control plane | **Worth exploring** | #873 is complete and #882 is adjacent, but residual duplication remains across control-plane validation, lane rendering, Nx metadata, selectors, and handwritten docs. Current onboarding still says five workspaces instead of six and references deleted paths. |

## Evidence by finding

### 1. Endpoint policy duplication

Relevant files:

- `packages/hevy-client/src/hevy-client-kubb.ts`
- `packages/core/src/utils/hevy-error-policy.ts`
- `packages/core/src/utils/error-policy.ts`
- `packages/node/src/utils/hevy-client-observability.ts`
- `packages/operations/src/workouts.ts`

Endpoint identity and policy are represented by independent lists or branches. A change can therefore drift between client retry behavior, Core read-miss handling, safe diagnostics, operations behavior, and Node metric normalization.

The central model must keep distinct policy facts rather than flattening them into one broad allowlist. Unknown endpoints must remain fail-closed, and diagnostic redaction must not be weakened.

### 2. Shared operations remain shallow

Relevant files:

- `packages/operations/src/workouts.ts`
- `packages/operations/src/index.ts`
- `packages/core/src/tools/*.ts`
- `packages/cli/src/commands/index.ts`

The operations workspace proves the desired seam through `workouts.list`, but most Core tools and CLI commands still orchestrate the curated Hevy client separately. Grow #872 domain by domain; adapters should retain argument parsing, presentation, and runtime observation rather than Hevy-domain workflow policy.

### 3. Validation repeats tests and builds

Relevant files:

- `project.json`
- `nx.json`
- `package.json`
- `repository/validation-lanes.json`
- `tests/package/*`
- `.github/workflows/build-and-test.yml`

Specialized contract, stdio, and CLI tests are all selected by unit and then executed again by their named lanes. The build/pack path also rebuilds Node and CLI artifacts inside package smoke work after earlier graph producers have run.

Disjointness must preserve complete coverage and focused debugging commands. Artifact consumers must reject stale output; this is not permission to remove custom policy checks or package-install smoke behavior.

### 4. Node lifecycle duplication

Relevant files:

- `packages/node/src/index.ts`
- `packages/node/src/utils/graceful-shutdown.ts`
- `packages/node/src/streamable-http.ts`
- `packages/node/src/index.test.ts`

`runStdioServer` and the HTTP runner repeat one substantial lifecycle implementation. A private lifecycle runner with two real transport adapters would improve locality without erasing transport-specific behavior.

### 5. Repeated deterministic test machinery

Relevant files:

- `tests/integration/mocked/hevy-mcp.mocked.integration.test.ts`
- `tests/integration/mocked/get-workout-count-events-mocked.integration.test.ts`
- `packages/core/src/tools/*.test.ts`
- `docs/testing-strategy.md`

This is renewed current-state evidence for #606. A shared test-support module should remain private, fail on leaked sessions/interceptors/network calls, and preserve visible failure diagnostics.

### 6. Response-contract implementation breadth

Relevant files:

- `packages/core/src/utils/response-contracts.ts`
- `packages/core/src/utils/response-contracts.test.ts`

Keep the existing deep public response interface. Explore compiling each validation schema once and organizing private domain implementations around shared pagination behavior. Preserve exact structured schemas and legacy text output.

### 7. Unmeasured Worker admission cost

Relevant files:

- `packages/worker/src/worker.ts`
- `packages/worker/src/worker.test.ts`
- `tests/performance/scenario.ts`
- `tests/performance/performance.test.ts`

The first deliverable is a representative repeated-request benchmark. Any reuse design must explicitly preserve credential revocation, tenant isolation, request isolation, and stateless transport semantics.

### 8. Residual control-plane drift

Relevant files:

- `scripts/control-plane-validation.mjs`
- `scripts/control-plane-models.mjs`
- `scripts/repository-control-plane.mjs`
- `scripts/render-validation-lanes.mjs`
- `repository/validation-lanes.json`
- `project.json`
- `docs/contributor-onboarding.md`
- `docs/testing-strategy.md`

`control-plane-validation.mjs` is 1,091 lines. Twenty-six of 28 mapped lanes repeat the same alias and Nx target name. Validation/rendering code rereads overlapping sources, while handwritten changing facts have drifted.

Derive simple one-to-one projections from one validated model seam. Preserve custom commands, cache exceptions, runtime/package policy, release policy, and the compiler-backed dependency checker as explicit policy.

## Recommended routing order

1. Define the endpoint-policy ownership and coordinate it with #928.
2. Add the measured validation baseline and artifact-flow slice to #882.
3. Decide whether to reopen #606 or file a narrowed successor.
4. Continue shared operations through #872 and Node lifecycle through #878.
5. File a focused response-contract implementation/benchmark issue if accepted.
6. Add the Worker benchmark requirement to #879 before any reuse design.
7. Route residual control-plane and documentation drift to #882 or a focused successor.

This is an ordering for maintainer leverage, not a requirement to combine the work into one branch or pull request.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Every finding above is marked accepted, deferred, or rejected with a short rationale.
- [ ] Every accepted finding has exactly one owning issue; existing issues are reused where their scope already matches.
- [ ] The endpoint-policy owner distinguishes retry, expected-absence, diagnostic-safety, and metric-identity facts and remains fail-closed for unknown endpoints.
- [ ] #882 records the cold/warm baseline and requires before/after execution counts and wall time without weakening validation.
- [ ] #606 is either reopened, replaced by a narrower issue, or remains closed with a current rationale that addresses the repeated setup still present.
- [ ] Response-contract work is preceded by an allocation/render benchmark and preserves externally visible contracts.
- [ ] #879 receives a repeated-request Worker benchmark before any validation or server reuse is approved.
- [ ] Residual control-plane/docs drift has an owner and generated/parity-checked projections replace only derivable duplication.
- [ ] Accepted runtime/package changes identify their Changeset cascade from `repository/topology.json`.
- [ ] No accepted item requires editing `packages/hevy-client/src/generated/` by hand.

## Guardrails

- Preserve runtime-neutral direction: `hevy-client → operations → core`, with Node, Worker, and CLI as independent adapters.
- Keep generated client internals private and regenerated from their source.
- Keep npm scripts as compatibility entrypoints while Nx owns graph/input/output/cache metadata.
- Preserve the custom compiler-backed package-policy check; generic tooling may complement but not silently replace it.
- Do not broaden safe diagnostic data while deduplicating endpoint/error policy.
- Do not add Worker credential caching or shared mutable state without revocation and isolation evidence.
- Do not turn this tracking issue into one large implementation pull request.

## Validation expectations

Each implementation issue should run the focused lane for its changed seam plus the repository baseline:

```text
mise exec -- npm run check
mise exec -- npm run check:types
mise exec -- npm run build
mise exec -- npm run test:pr
mise exec -- npm run test:performance
mise exec -- npm run check:changeset
```

Performance-oriented work must publish the exact before/after command, cold/warm state, execution count, wall time, and any correctness trade-off.

## Non-goals

- Reopening completed roadmap issues merely to duplicate their accepted scope.
- Creating a second operations, lifecycle, Worker-routing, or validation model beside #872, #878, #879, or #882.
- Removing safety, release, package, privacy, or compatibility checks to improve timing.
- Designing a Worker cache before measuring the actual hot path.
- Splitting cohesive modules only because they are large.

## Review relationship

This is a current-checkout follow-up to the completed synthesis in #865 and portfolio decision in #866. It records what remains observable after subsequent architecture and Nx work, and routes those deltas into the live backlog.
